method: Read primary pages and paper text; search snippets are not verification. Duplicate hosted captions are not independent datasets.

claims.wording: Opportunity's final region was Perseverance Valley, on Endeavour Crater's inner western rim.
claims.caveat: Pancam and later orbital observations support the region, not our authored map coordinates.

claims.wording: Tau describes atmospheric optical opacity; it is not a deposited dust-layer thickness.

evidence.locator: Paper p.1 Nomenclature; p.4 section II.A

claims.caveat: Dimensionless; value depends on observational context. Avoid converting it into a linear percentage.

claims.wording: JPL gives roughly 0.5 as an average tau at Opportunity's site.
claims.caveat: Contextual site average, not a universal clear-sky value or confirmed opening-day telemetry.

claims.wording: Opportunity's last reported tau was approximately 10.8 on June 10, 2018.
claims.caveat: Two documents reference the same mission observation; not independent measurements. Not proof of the storm's eventual global maximum.

claims.wording: The later atmospheric paper describes Opportunity's extreme opacity as a lower limit above 10.7.

evidence.locator: Paper p.4, section II.A, second paragraph

claims.caveat: Consistent with an approximate 10.8 report; do not invent excess precision or compare directly with different wavelengths/sites.
claims.runtime_use: Technical caveat, not necessary player copy

claims.wording: MRO first detected the developing storm on May 30, 2018; Opportunity reduced operations by June 6.

evidence.locator: Original story posted on June 8; paragraph beginning Opportunity's power levels

claims.caveat: Page header is July 26 because it accumulates updates; use the dated June section.

claims.wording: On June 10, Opportunity still transmitted; science operations remained suspended.

evidence.locator: Updated at 4:30 p.m. PDT on June 10, first paragraph

claims.caveat: Reported battery sufficiency to communicate at that time is not a later battery state-of-charge record.

claims.wording: NASA identifies June 10, 2018 as the last communication date.
claims.caveat: Mission records cross-check the date; both are NASA records, not independent telemetry datasets.

claims.wording: PIA22929 is a partial Pancam frame exposed around 09:30 PDT on June 10, sol 5111.
claims.caveat: Exposure time differs from relay and Earth receipt; no exact shutdown time follows from it.

claims.wording: In PIA22929, noise accounts for bright speckles and missing transmission data accounts for the black lower area.

evidence.locator: Description, camera noise and interrupted transmission paragraph

claims.caveat: The dark received area is not the same thing as the unreceived region. Preserve both without generative filling.

claims.wording: PIA22929's caption places relay at about 09:45 PDT and Earth receipt at about 10:05 PDT.
claims.caveat: Approximate Earth time-standard labels as published, not Mars local time. No instant simultaneous scene beat.

claims.wording: PIA22930 contains later exposures, around 09:33 PDT; their full-size frames were never received.
claims.caveat: Thumbnails arrived before the last partial frame. The caption's EDT a.m. parenthetical is inconsistent; use PDT or explicitly converted UTC.

claims.wording: PIA22930 uses left/right Pancam views through 440 nm and 750 nm filters.
claims.caveat: Not natural-color imagery; enlargement cannot recover absent detail.

claims.wording: The final panorama combines 354 frames acquired May 13–June 10, sols 5084–5111.
claims.caveat: Multi-date assembled observation, not one instantaneous storm view.

claims.wording: PIA22909 is approximate true color; PIA22908 is false color; some mosaic panels lack a complete filter set.

evidence.locator: Description, approximate color and filter paragraphs

claims.caveat: Related products of the same panorama, not independent corroborating observations.

claims.wording: PIA22521 depicts simulated skies at tau 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11.
claims.caveat: Simulation, not six sequential rover photographs or a calibrated brightness curve.

claims.wording: By June 19 the event was classified as planet-encircling in JPL's June 20 update.

evidence.locator: Updated at 1:20 p.m. PDT on June 20, first paragraph

claims.caveat: Retrospective paper p.5 describes June 20 circumnavigation. Use June 19–20 or attribution; do not silently pick a universal timestamp.

claims.wording: After contact was lost, engineers considered low-power, clock and uploss fault scenarios.
claims.caveat: Low-power entry was an engineering assumption. These are not confirmed final diagnoses or player-selected historical switches.

claims.wording: JPL's June 12 explanation described assumed low-power behavior that shut down subsystems while retaining a mission clock.

evidence.locator: Updated at 6:30 p.m. PDT on June 12

claims.caveat: Its 24 V reference is voltage, not battery charge percent; describe as an assumption made after a failed contact attempt.
claims.runtime_use: Basis for labeled simplified conservation choices

claims.wording: Clearing skies did not establish clean solar panels or a recovered rover.

evidence.locator: Oct.11 update, possible dust layer and unknown quantity
Caption, unknown array dust and limits of orbital observation

claims.caveat: Atmospheric opacity and deposited dust are separate. Later images cannot determine array dust amount.

claims.wording: On September 11, commands increased from three times weekly to multiple times daily while passive listening continued.

evidence.locator: Updated at 2:45 p.m. PDT on Sept.11

claims.caveat: Operational increase after two MARCI tau estimates below 1.5; this is not a physical universal recovery threshold.

claims.wording: The team kept trying through a hoped-for November–January dust-clearing season.
claims.caveat: Expected winds and cleaning were uncertain, not a documented successful cleaning or rescue.

claims.wording: January 2019 commands tested possible radio failures or clock offset as well as sweep-and-beep.

evidence.locator: Main text, three possible scenarios and proposed remedies

claims.caveat: Unlikely hypotheses, not known component failures. Over 600 attempts then and over 1,000 commands later are different time/count descriptions.

claims.wording: NASA reported more than 1,000 recovery commands and declared the mission complete February 13, 2019.

evidence.locator: Mission conclusion, paragraph beginning The Opportunity rover stopped communicating

claims.caveat: Use aggregate campaign summary. Do not invent a timestamped record for each displayed command.

claims.wording: The final command attempt was late February 12 in the JPL account, before the February 13 announcement.

evidence.locator: Image caption beginning Late on Feb.12, 2019

claims.caveat: Keep the local-date wording; do not assert an unprovided exact time or conflate it with the June loss of contact.

claims.wording: HiRISE observed Opportunity on September 20, 2018 in ESP_056955_1775.
claims.caveat: Same orbital observation in two presentations; no independent confirmation of rover internal condition.

claims.wording: The HiRISE record lists center latitude -2.335 degrees and east longitude 354.652 degrees; full map-projected imagery is north-up at 25 cm/pixel.

evidence.locator: Acquisition metadata: Latitude centered, Longitude East, Map projected scale

claims.caveat: Image-center metadata is not exact rover GPS. Do not apply full-product pixel scale to downsampled context JPEGs.

claims.wording: Spirit and Opportunity both depended on solar power; Ingenuity also used a solar panel and batteries.

evidence.locator: How They Did It, solar-powered twins
In Depth, solar panels and winter discussion
Bytes and Cake, daily solar-panel and battery tests

claims.caveat: Shared energy dependence, not identical hardware or a common cause of mission endings. Ingenuity's flight-ending damage is a different event.

claims.wording: Opportunity's end-of-mission odometry was 45.16 km.

evidence.locator: In Depth, paragraph beginning When NASA declared

claims.caveat: Historical final distance, not a claim that it still holds a present-day record.

claims.wording: The storm's global peak occurred after Opportunity's final contact; other spacecraft continued observing it.

evidence.locator: Paper abstract and section II.A, pp.4–5

claims.caveat: Do not transfer Curiosity's 880 nm opacity or REMS temperature/UV curves to Opportunity's site.

claims.wording: A complete numerical battery-percent or shutdown trajectory after June 10 is established by these sources.
claims.caveat: Not found in the sources checked. Do not ship this claim; source communication loss does not prove zero charge or an exact final failure.

claims.wording: The exact final rover heading, pitch/roll and full articulation pose are established for direct game placement.
claims.caveat: Region and surrounding forms are supported; exact final body-frame pose was not found in the records checked. Do not substitute valley slope or image solar angles.

claims.wording: 22 Wh is a primary-verified final battery charge for this pack.
claims.caveat: This figure appeared in secondary coverage; a primary, context-complete energy record was not established here. It would describe energy, not a battery percentage. Omit from runtime pending a primary record.

claims.wording: Player conservation choices should illustrate demand reduction without a savable alternative ending.

evidence.locator: June8 science suspension and June12 assumed low-power explanation

claims.caveat: Design abstraction, not historical command reenactment. Do not assign invented watts, a guaranteed survival strategy or required heater shutdown.

claims.wording: Use a period break before the later recovery campaign and return beside the silent rover.
claims.caveat: The spirit and transitions are fiction. Preserve the fixed historical outcome without blaming the player.

claims.wording: High opacity by itself proves destructive surface winds or physical rover damage.
claims.caveat: Unsupported inference. No exact wind-speed/impact/damage claim is selected.

claims.wording: Authentic Opportunity recordings of the 2018 storm were located.
claims.caveat: Not found in the sources checked. Any later designed audio, Earth analogue or other-mission recording needs clear labeling and rights.

claims.wording: The source parenthetical 12:33 a.m. EDT is consistent with 09:33 a.m. PDT.
claims.caveat: The offsets differ by three hours; the EDT a.m. text is inconsistent. Preserve original record; use published PDT. 16:33 UTC / 12:33 p.m. EDT are explicit time-zone conversions, not new acquisition evidence.

claims.wording: The final-panorama caption's June 3, 2018 / sol 5014 pairing is ready for runtime use.
claims.caveat: Internally inconsistent with its own March sols 5015–5038 and May/June sols 5084–5111. Omit this date-sol pair; no guessed correction is selected.
